text:
maria_perf: Kicking off a trace-playback run to validate kernel selection + batching parity vs prod traces. Goal: reproduce the perf regression from yesterday and rule out nondeterministic KV cache effects.
aj_ops: SGTM. what's the sampling slice? full-traffic or stratified?
sasha_ml: prefer stratified by model + seq_len bucket. small models + short seqs dominated the regression in the flame graphs.
maria_perf: plan: 0.5% sample stratified by model, 3 seq_len buckets (<128, 128-1024, >1024), deterministic seed for ordering. anonymize user ids first.
kevin_runtime: +1 on deterministic seed. make sure the kernel choice path is logged (kernel_id + heuristics input). we had a kernel fallback spike in the tail yesterday.
maria_perf: logging snippet I'm using: ```KERNELOPTS kernel_id=%s heuristics={batch_size:%d,seq_len:%d,kv_hit:%d}``` will include this in bench output.
aj_ops: for anonymization we used the quick-hash approach last quarter: `sha256(user_id + stable_salt)` then truncate. keeps determinism without PII. ok to reuse?
sasha_ml: yep. confirm salt stored in vault. it's only needed for deterministic shard splits. also strip prompt tokens >2000 chars to avoid leaking long text.
kevin_runtime: noticed nondeterminism earlier came from two places: 1) async KV warmup race, 2) floating-point kernel selection tie-breaker. we should force synchronous KV warmup and a deterministic tie-break on kernel score during the run.
maria_perf: good catch. I'll enable `--kv-warmup=sync` and `--kernel-tiebreak=seeded` for this run. command: ```./traceplay --sample 0.005 --seed 1337 --kv-warmup=sync --kernel-tiebreak=seeded --anon-salt=redwood-v1```
aj_ops: bench-bot will post tail latency + p50/p95/p99 per kernel_id, and compare to the golden baseline. bench-bot: please create an apples-to-apples comparison report (same input order & same batching heuristic) and annotate any kernel_id mismatches.
bench-bot: running run_id=2035004321. uploading artifacts to s3://redwood-bench/2035004321/ . will post metrics once aggregation completes. :gear:
sasha_ml: if parity fails, let's do a delta trace: replay the exact sequence but force kernel selection to the golden kernel and see if latency matches. that isolates selection vs execution perf.
kevin_runtime: also include a microbenchmark: single-kernel perf for the top 3 kernels with the same batch/seq_len mix as the trace. real kernels sometimes regress due to compiler flags.
maria_perf: noted. timeline: run starts in 10m, expect initial metrics in ~30m. will post logs + flame graphs here. please review asap if you get alerts.
aj_ops: will monitor infra. @kevin_runtime @sasha_ml keep phones nearby in case we need a quick rollback. :iphone:
kevin_runtime: one more: add `--kv-metrics=per-request` so we can see cache hit/miss per request window. yesterday aggregate numbers hid a pathological cohort.
maria_perf: enabled. also added an eval harness compare: sample 200 prompts run through both golden and experiment models and diff token-level timings. small script: ```python diff_eval.py --left s3://golden/trace.json --right s3://2035004321/trace.json --out diffs.json```
sasha_ml: perfect. would like to add a sanity check for output determinism (token sequences equal) before trusting perf diffs. if outputs differ we need to separate quality variance from perf changes.
aj_ops: +1. bench-bot: please mark the run with tags: [deterministic_seed, anon, stratified_sample].
bench-bot: tags applied. posting interim summary: p50 delta +2ms, p95 +18ms for kernel_id=kc_17. attaching first 10 kernel selection logs to thread.
maria_perf: seeing kc_17 get chosen more often at higher seq_len buckets than golden. digging into heuristics input (batch_size & kv_hit). early hypothesis: KV cache warmup async was causing some misses in prod->golden mapping and our forced sync changes selection frequency.
kevin_runtime: that aligns: kc_17 has better perf when kv_hit=1. if our synthetic run forced extra misses, selection could flip. check per-request kv_hit rate in the same time window.
sasha_ml: if parity still off after making KV behavior identical, then GPU kernel regression is likely. we'll run kernel-only microbench and open a perf-compiler ticket.
maria_perf: quick action items: 1) I'll upload anonymized trace + kernel logs to the bench artifacts. 2) @kevin_runtime do kernel microbench for kc_17 and kc_12 with exact batch/seq profile. 3) @sasha_ml run output-determinism check and token-diff.
kevin_runtime: on it. starting microbench now. will post logs and perf counters (sm_eff, l2_bw) to the artifact folder.
aj_ops: infra looks stable. no capacity alerts.
bench-bot: final aggregates for run_id=2035004321: p50 +1.9ms, p95 +17.6ms, p99 +42ms; kv_hit_rate overall 87% vs golden 91%; kernel_selection_changes: 73 switches (top: kc_12->kc_17).
maria_perf: initial conclusion: bulk of regression explained by reduced kv_hit_rate in the sampled window which nudged kernel selection to kc_17 for long seqs; microbench shows kc_17 is ~6% slower on mixed batch sizes (matches p95 delta).
sasha_ml: thanks. let's open follow-ups: - infra: investigate what caused kv_hit drop in prod window (cache eviction/trace cohort). - runtime: make kernel tiebreak deterministic permanently. - perf: revert the compiler flags that changed kc_17 if microbench confirms regression.
kevin_runtime: filing runtime PR to set deterministic tie-break and add more granular kernel telemetry.
maria_perf: filing infra ticket with timeline & trace slice. will close loop here after fixes. thanks everyone. :white_check_mark:
